name: masked-notes
description: Two entities carrying a hidden field, differing only in whether the caller may read them at all — so the hidden field's NAME can be shown indistinguishable from an unknown one for BOTH an authorized and a policy-denied caller. The carve-out being tested: a hidden field's name must stay indistinguishable from an unknown one, because Task 8 excludes it from the published document while the rest of the declared shape is public. The denied half exists because a denied decision carries an EMPTY mask, so resolving the policy only after the query parser made the two answers differ (422 for an undeclared field, 403 for a declared-hidden one) for exactly the caller most likely to be probing.

notes.description: A note with one field the descriptor author marked confidential. Every rule permits every caller, so a fact about the hidden field's name is not also a fact about access.

ledgers.description: The same shape as 'notes', with NO 'list' or 'get' rule at all — so default-deny refuses every read outright, which is the only way to reach a DENIED decision for a lister. A role test like "'auditor' in @user.roles" cannot do it: a rule compiles to a row-level USING predicate, so a caller without the role gets an ALLOW carrying a predicate that matches nothing (200 with an empty page), never IsDenied. A caller must still hold the 'ledgers:read' scope to get this far, since a scope refusal answers a different slug from the endpoint filter and never resolves a policy.
